words.etymology: From Proto-Albanian *pa ̊, from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂(y)- (“to herd, watch over”). Cognate to Sanskrit पति (pā́ti-, “to herd, watch (over)”). A suppletive verb, which occurs in the participle and the aorist and as in the tempora and modi derived from these stems.

words.etymology:
From Proto-Albanian *apsera or *asper(a), perhaps representing a contamination of *aps, reflected in Ancient Greek ἄψ (áps, “backwards”), a variant of Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó (“off, away”), with Proto-Indo-European *h₂épero-. Cognate to Sanskrit अपर (ápara, “posterior, later, following”), Gothic 𐌰𐍆𐌰𐍂 (afar, “after”), Old Persian 𐎠𐎱𐎼 (a-p-r /⁠apara⁠/, “later, after”), Avestan 𐬀𐬞𐬀𐬭𐬀 (apara, “more behind, later”).
Or possibly from Latin affīnis.
Alternatively, from a + -fër.

words.etymology: A derivative of vjet (“last year”), variant of vit (“year”), from Proto-Albanian *weta, from Proto-Indo-European *wétos (“year”), contaminated with Latin vetus, veteris. Compare Lithuanian vẽtušas (“old”, archaic), Old Church Slavonic ветъхъ (vetŭxŭ, “old, ancient”). Attributed directly to Latin veterem by Orel.
